instruction: I'm getting an error "python: command not found" when trying to run Python scripts with 'python' instead of 'python3'. Could you create an alias in my shell configuration so that 'python' points to 'python3'?

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding an alias 'python=python3' to .bashrc file. Evaluator checks if the alias line exists in .bashrc using grep. Similar complexity to the original conda task - both involve adding shell initialization code to .bashrc.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic is semantically sound - it correctly verifies that an alias was added to shell configuration

The grep pattern ['\"]?python3['\"]? is actually flexible and accepts multiple valid formats: no quotes (alias python=python3), single quotes (alias python='python3'), and double quotes (alias python=\"python3\")
Data flow is correct: getter extracts command output -> metric compares exact match -> expected value '1\n' indicates success

Minor limitation: evaluator only checks ~/.bashrc, but instruction says 'shell configuration' which could include ~/.bash_profile, ~/.zshrc, etc. However, ~/.bashrc is the most common location for Ubuntu systems
No postconfig issues - .bashrc file persists and is accessible after task completion
The expected value '1\n' is semantically correct for the grep command output
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider checking multiple shell config files if the instruction asks for 'shell configuration' generically: ~/.bashrc, ~/.bash_profile, ~/.profile, or ~/.zshrc depending on shell type
Alternative: verify functionality by running 'which python' or 'python --version' after sourcing config to confirm python command resolves correctly
